title: Stage 04 validation - CT priority router adaptive series v4.1 through v4.7
declaration: This is an adaptive experiment series, not a set of independent prospective validations.

Seven router versions were evaluated against six nominally prospective benchmark cohorts. Each version after v4.1 was designed from the observed failure mode of the previous version, and in the later versions the previous cohort's outcome was consumed directly as development data.

Consequently NO metric reported by ANY version of this series is an unbiased estimator of out-of-sample performance. Each 'prospective' result is conditioned on every prior cohort outcome the designer had already seen.

No family-wise error rate control, Bonferroni correction, alpha-spending schedule or any other multiplicity correction was pre-registered or applied. With six evaluations against per-scroll recall and efficiency gates, the nominal per-version thresholds are not the effective error rates of the series.
Six of the seven versions failed. The one that passed, v4.1, is the first version tried, which is the only version in the series for which the cohort was genuinely unseen at design time.

series_extent.additional_development_stage_failures_no: v4.3 recorded two development-stage failures (model-v43 and model-v43-physical-morphology-r01, both V43_DEVELOPMENT_FAILED_DO_NOT_EVALUATE_V4) before its source-holdout r02 configuration was frozen for the one shot. Counting development rounds the series contains eight recorded failures.
series_extent.elapsed_measured: approximately 8 h 17 min, all within the single calendar day 2026-07-24
series_extent.correction_to_audit: docs/PIPELINE_AUDIT_20260724.md FIX-15 describes this series as 'six prospective benchmarks over nine days'. Both receipt timestamps and git first-commit dates for every ct-priority-router-v4x finding directory place the entire series inside 2026-07-24, spanning roughly eight and a quarter hours. The compression makes the multiplicity concern more acute, not less: six prospective cohorts were consumed faster than any of them could have been independently re-collected.

cohort_disjointness.finding: The cohorts are NOT fully disjoint. Two separate violations were verified by comparing (scroll_id, official_surface_id, surface_y_x_level0) tuples across all six frozen control sets.

violations.description: v4.1 and v4.2 consumed the identical cohort. Both ran against MULTISCROLL_TRANSFER_V3 with the same controls_sha256 4b1c39155190fa..., the same 300 frozen controls.
violations.consequence: MULTISCROLL_TRANSFER_V3 is not a prospective cohort for v4.2. v4.2 was designed after reading v4.1's V3 result and was then scored on those same controls.
violations.acknowledged_in_repo: V42_PROMOTION_DECISION.json sets v3_may_be_reused_for_tuning: false and requires a new disjoint transfer benchmark for any replacement, so the reuse is acknowledged policy - but it happened.

violations.description: MULTISCROLL_TRANSFER_V6 (consumed by v4.5) reuses 40 of MULTISCROLL_TRANSFER_V3's 300 controls at byte-identical coordinates: 20 from PHerc1667 surface w023_20240304161941_2um and 20 from PHercParis4 surface w01_20230702185753_r15, with matching expected_class on all 40.
violations.root_cause: V4, V5 and V6 were each frozen with exclusion_radius_level0_pixels: null and excluded_frozen_control_count: 0, whereas V3, V7 and V8 used 176.0 with 600 and 900 exclusions respectively. V4 and V5 escaped overlap only because they happened to draw different scrolls; V6 returned to PHerc1667 and PHercParis4 and collided.
violations.consequence: v4.5's V6 result is partly retrospective on controls that v4.1 and v4.2 had already been measured against.

cohort_disjointness.verified_disjoint_pairs: V3, V4, V5, V7 and V8 are mutually disjoint at exact-location granularity. V7's source plan explicitly asserts v7_evaluation_controls_spatially_disjoint_from_v46_calibration: true.

versions.previous_failure_addressed: the frozen v3 fixed 240 um window sent every valid official control to Tier C
versions.caveat: positive_v3_tier_a_recall was 0.0 across all three scrolls; all 300 controls landed in TIER_B_SHADOW_REVIEW. The pass is a preservation pass with zero workload reduction.

versions.derivation_quote: preserved every positive control... but it also sent every confounder to the same review queue. Its recall was safe and its workload reduction was zero.

versions.previous_failure_addressed: v4.2 memorization of surfaces and scanners
versions.derivation_quote: v4.2 used 5,236 texture variables, PCA and an RBF SVM. Its large fitted-versus-grouped gap showed memorization of surfaces and scanners.

versions.headline_metric: positive recall and confound B2 rate, minima across scrolls
versions.headline_value: min recall 0.94 vs 0.95; min confound B2 rate 0.02 vs 0.15
versions.previous_failure_addressed: v4.3 V4 recall shortfall (recorded only in the cross-version narrative, not in the v4.4 artifacts)
versions.additional_caveat_field: semantic_provenance_caveat - Public prediction maps are frozen features, not ground truth; their training provenance may overlap public labeled domains.
versions.receipt_defect: EXECUTION_RECEIPT.json carries only status EXECUTED_ONCE with no timestamp field.

versions.cohort_prospective_note: 40 of the 300 controls are byte-identical reuses of MULTISCROLL_TRANSFER_V3 controls. See cohort_disjointness.violations.V6_OVERLAPS_V3.
versions.headline_metric: positive recall per scroll; confound B2 rate per scroll
versions.gate: recall >= 0.95 and confound B2 rate >= 0.15 per scroll
versions.previous_failure_addressed: v4.4 V5 failure; the design pivots to per-model-family calibration with a B1_PRESERVE_ALL fallback
versions.contamination_note: The v4.4 failure cohort V5 became v4.5's development set. The prospective cohort of one version is the training set of the next.

versions.headline_value_note: The 1.0 for PHerc0139 is a B1_PRESERVE_ALL no-op, not a routing result.
versions.previous_failure_addressed: v4.5's PHerc0139 recall collapse to 0.68, encoded structurally by setting PHerc0139 to B1_PRESERVE_ALL with reason NO_DEVELOPMENT_OPERATING_POINT_MET_RECALL_AND_EFFICIENCY

versions.headline_value_note: Two of the three 1.0 values are B1_PRESERVE_ALL no-ops. The single calibrated surface, PHercParis4, missed the gate by 0.01.
versions.previous_failure_addressed: v4.6 V7 per-scroll gate failures; v4.7 retains only the surface routers that passed both prospective V7 gates
versions.derivation_quote: Freeze v4.7 from the prospective V7 result. Only surface routers that passed both prospective V7 gates remain calibrated.
versions.contamination_note: This is the most explicit selection-on-the-outcome in the series: v4.7's surface set is literally defined as the subset of surfaces whose V7 result was good. Its V8 numbers for that subset are therefore selected, not prospective.

how_to_read_this_series: v4.1 is the only version whose cohort was unseen at design time. Its result is the only one in the series that can be read at close to face value, and even it reports zero workload reduction.
v4.2 through v4.7 each had access to at least one prior cohort outcome at design time, and v4.5 and v4.7 consumed a prior cohort as development data outright.
The correct summary of the series is: no CT priority router in this family has been shown to reduce review workload while preserving positive controls on a genuinely unseen cohort.
v4.1 remains the operational default and v4.2 through v4.7 remain frozen negative results.
non_claims: This declaration does not invalidate any individual version; it states the conditions under which the numbers may be read.
This declaration does not establish that a corrected series would have produced a different outcome.
This declaration does not establish correct geometry, ink, letters, or First Letters.
This declaration makes no external generalization claim.
corrections_to_the_source_audit: The audit describes the series as spanning nine days. Receipt timestamps and git first-commit dates place it entirely inside 2026-07-24, spanning roughly 8 h 17 min.

The audit describes six disjoint prospective benchmarks. Two disjointness violations were verified: v4.1 and v4.2 shared the identical V3 cohort, and V6 reuses 40 of V3's 300 controls at byte-identical coordinates.
The audit implies a v4.2-to-v4.7 series of six. Including v4.1 the family is seven versions over six cohorts, of which six versions failed.
